name: Epaphroditus (from Philippi)
title: The Messenger of the Philippians
summary: Epaphroditus was a faithful Christian from the church in Philippi who was sent to Paul in Rome with financial support. He became seriously ill during his stay but recovered and was sent back with Paul's letter to the Philippians. Paul refers to him with great warmth as his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier.

keyEvents.title: Sent from Philippi to Paul
keyEvents.description: The church in Philippi sent Epaphroditus to Rome with gifts and support for Paul, who was imprisoned. He was also to serve the apostle's needs.

keyEvents.title: Serious Illness
keyEvents.description: During his stay in Rome, Epaphroditus became critically ill. News of his sickness reached Philippi, and he was worried that the church was anxious about him.

keyEvents.title: God's Mercy and Healing
keyEvents.description: God showed mercy to Epaphroditus and healed him from his illness, which also spared Paul further grief.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Praise and Recommendation
keyEvents.description: Paul described Epaphroditus as his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, and urged the Philippians to receive him with joy and honor such men.

keyEvents.title: Bearer of the Letter to the Philippians
keyEvents.description: Epaphroditus was sent back to Philippi and was likely the one who delivered Paul's letter to the church there.
